message.content:
**Kings of France in the 18th Century** | Reign | Monarch | Key Notes | |-------|---------|-----------| | **1715 – 1774** | **Louis XV** (born 1710, died 1774) | • Succeeded his great‑uncle Louis XIV upon the latter’s death.
• His long reign saw relative peace, economic growth, and the flourishing of French arts (“Age of Enlightenment”).
• He faced increasing fiscal crises and political opposition toward the end of his life. | | **1774 – 1792** | **Louis XVI** (born 1754, executed 1793) | • Became king at age 20 following Louis XV’s death.
• Initially ruled under the Regency of Philippe Égalité (his father, Duke of Orléans).
• His reign culminated in the French Revolution; he attempted reforms but ultimately failed to quell unrest.
• Deposed in 1792, imprisoned, and guillotined in January 1793. | *After 1792 the Bourbon monarchy ceased to exist—France entered the Revolutionary era, followed briefly by Napoléon Bonaparte’s Consulate/Empire.* So, throughout the entire 18th century, France had **two reigning kings:** *Louis XV* and *Louis XVI*.
